blocks.orig: The cheetah is an incredible species of big cat and is known as the fastest land mammal on Earth.
blocks.html: The cheetah is a remarkable big cat, famous for being the fastest land mammal on the planet.

blocks.orig: In Tanzania, there is a subspecies of cheetah named the East African cheetah that lives in the country’s grasslands and savannahs.
blocks.html: Tanzania is home to a cheetah subspecies called the East African cheetah, which roams the country’s savannahs and grasslands.

blocks.orig: In this article, we’ll tell you everything you need to know about the East African cheetah, including its habitat, the threats to its survival, and what conservation efforts are being put in place to protect it.
blocks.html: This article covers all you need to know about the East African cheetah: where it lives, what threatens its survival and which conservation measures are being taken to safeguard it.

blocks.orig: East African cheetahs weigh between 69.9 and 74.8 kilograms (154 and 165 pounds) and have a head-and-body length of about 1.1 to 1.4 meters (3.6 to 4.5 feet). Typically, males are larger than females.
blocks.html: An East African cheetah weighs somewhere between 69.9 and 74.8 kilograms (154 and 165 pounds), with a head-and-body length of roughly 1.1 to 1.4 metres (3.6 to 4.5 feet). Males are usually bigger than females.

blocks.orig: Tanzania’s East African cheetahs are somewhat longer but lighter. They can weigh between 49.9 and 59 kilograms (110 and 130 pounds) and be 2 to 2.2 meters (6.6 to 7.2 feet) long.
blocks.html: The East African cheetahs in Tanzania tend to be slightly longer yet lighter. Their weight ranges from 49.9 to 59 kilograms (110 to 130 pounds) and their length from 2 to 2.2 metres (6.6 to 7.2 feet).

blocks.orig: East African cheetahs have a white-yellowish to tannish coat. Typically, their fur is shorter and thinner, while some may have thick, coarse fur on their bellies.
blocks.html: The coat of an East African cheetah ranges from white-yellowish to tannish. As a rule the fur is short and thin, although some animals have thick, coarse hair on the belly.

blocks.orig: Except for its white underbelly, it has several circular black dots, some of which can be seen on the chest and neck. The spots blend together toward the tip of the tail to produce four to fourteen dark rings and a white tuft.
blocks.html: Apart from the white underbelly, the body is covered in round black spots, some of them visible on the chest and neck. Towards the end of the tail the spots merge into four to fourteen dark rings, finishing in a white tuft.

blocks.orig: Its tear scars extend from the corners of its eyes to its mouth, which helps to diffuse the sunlight’s glare on its comparatively large, thick eyes.
blocks.html: Running from the corners of the eyes down to the mouth are the tear marks, which help reduce the glare of the sun on the cheetah’s relatively large, thick eyes.

blocks.orig: Cheetahs are primarily found in the scrub forests, grasslands, savannahs, open fields, steppes, and desert environments of East Africa, where they can find prey that is suited for them to use as their primary hunting grounds.
blocks.html: In East Africa, cheetahs live mostly in scrub forest, grassland, savannah, open plains, steppe and desert – places where suitable prey is available and which serve as their main hunting grounds.

blocks.orig: A few are also found in mountain ranges, coastal regions, and lakeshores.
blocks.html: Smaller numbers live in mountain ranges, along the coast and on lakeshores.

blocks.orig: The majority of the cheetah’s range lies between northern Tanzania and southern Kenya.
blocks.html: Most of the cheetah’s range stretches from northern Tanzania into southern Kenya.

blocks.orig: East African cheetahs are mainly active during the day, making them one of the few apex predators in Africa to hunt during the day instead of nocturnally.
blocks.html: The East African cheetah is chiefly active in daylight, which makes it one of the few apex predators in Africa that hunts by day rather than by night.

blocks.orig: It usually eats medium-sized or large mammalian herbivores, such as antelopes, impala, gazelles, wildebeest, and guinea fowl.
blocks.html: Its usual prey consists of medium-sized or large plant-eating mammals – antelopes, impala, gazelles and wildebeest – along with guinea fowl.

blocks.orig: The poaching, habitat loss, and fragmentation taking place are the main factors that contribute to the cheetah’s endangerment.
blocks.html: Poaching, the loss of habitat and the fragmentation of what remains are the chief reasons the cheetah’s survival is under threat.

blocks.orig: Infectious disease affects cheetahs in the Serengeti and the Masai Mara, but it doesn’t pose a serious threat to the free-roaming cheetahs in East Africa.
blocks.html: In the Serengeti and the Masai Mara, cheetahs do suffer from infectious disease, yet for the free-roaming animals of East Africa this isn’t a serious danger.

blocks.orig: Conservation of the East African Cheetah
blocks.html: Protecting the East African cheetah

blocks.orig: Despite the cheetah’s many reserves and national parks, its population is still declining.
blocks.html: Even with the many reserves and national parks within the cheetah’s range, its numbers keep falling.

blocks.orig: The Mara-Meru Cheetah Project, the Serengeti Cheetah Project, Action for Cheetahs in Kenya, and the Tanzania Cheetah Conservation Program are just a few of the conservation initiatives being undertaken to prevent the extinction of the cheetah.
blocks.html: Among the conservation initiatives working to keep the cheetah from extinction are the Mara-Meru Cheetah Project, the Serengeti Cheetah Project, Action for Cheetahs in Kenya and the Tanzania Cheetah Conservation Program.

blocks.orig: The East African cheetah is a beautiful mammal that can be found roaming the incredible landscape of Tanzania and other eastern and southern parts of Africa.
blocks.html: A graceful animal, the East African cheetah roams the magnificent landscapes of Tanzania as well as other parts of eastern and southern Africa.

blocks.orig: While it is an endangered species, many efforts are being made to protect this incredible creature.
blocks.html: Although the species is endangered, a great deal of work is being done to protect this remarkable cat.
